canal_p04_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_001.text: Wei Xiu piloted the mail boat with one hand on the ordinary tiller and the other keeping a biscuit away from a persistent gull. An Ru sat forward with the packet. Yue offered ginger from her food bag before remembering the pilot's dislike. Wei Xiu looked wounded by the forgetfulness, then accepted the biscuit instead. The boat left the canal's careful little arguments behind and entered a river broad enough to make them seem both less important and harder to avoid.

canal_p04_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_002.text: At the first bend, Wei Xiu pointed to an old stone marker left above the water. Yue remembered the empty ferry's circles and the people who had learned to stop mistaking a place for a promise that could never change. She said the new canal notice had made another old agreement larger than its beginning. The pilot asked whether it also had a rotten pin. Yue laughed and described Bao's crane support. 'Then take a carpenter's answer seriously before an archivist makes it sound elegant,' Wei Xiu said.

canal_p04_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_003.text: The official archive passage fare had been entered in the canal's ordinary operating book, apart from the ninety-six-copper repair order. Luo had given the pilot the paid passage receipt before they left. Wei Xiu checked its return allowance and put it in her dry box. She would not be asked to carry every later messenger for free because this first journey served a common cause. Yue watched the simple exchange finish, then settled back to enjoy a trip whose cost somebody had actually arranged.

canal_p04_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_004.text: An Ru read Pei's offered recollection while the boat passed an orchard bank. She smiled at the description of blue binding thread and asked Yue what she thought it proved. Yue gave the limited answer. The archivist nodded, then asked whether she thought Pei was lying about the missing heading. Yue said no. An honest memory could still mistake a bundle. An Ru folded the letter and watched the trees. 'That answer will save us from insulting several people before lunch.'

canal_p04_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_005.text: A family on the bank waved the mail boat down with a red scarf. Wei Xiu recognized their usual signal and approached the ordinary landing rather than guessing it meant danger. They had a package of dried persimmons for a daughter at the archive school. An Ru made room beside her packet after the pilot accepted the scheduled parcel fee. The family's errand had nothing to do with the canal, which made Yue strangely happy. Their boat could carry more than one kind of necessary journey.

canal_p04_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_006.text: The daughter met them at the valley steps and complained that her father packed persimmons before she finished the previous batch. She was carrying a stack of public reading boards higher than her chin. Yue took the top two while An Ru kept the canal packet dry. The girl showed them the archive's temporary entrance. A roof repair had closed the front stairs. Yue remembered Pei's old transfer during another roof repair and hoped this building did not require every document to learn a new route each time rain found a joint.

canal_p04_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_007.text: The archive smelled of paste, old cedar and somebody's overcooked rice. An Ru paused at the entrance to read the temporary shelf-transfer notice. A newer storage list had moved several canal registers from the western room to a dry upper cabinet. The receiving number still existed, though its address had changed. Yue had imagined finding the book exactly where the old index promised. The archive was a workplace, not a preserved memory of the day a clerk last wrote a label.

canal_p04_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_008.text: A junior clerk apologized for the moving shelves before either visitor complained. He had been accused of losing three household packets during the roof work, all later found in their recorded temporary cabinet. An Ru asked for the transfer sheet rather than his defense. Its signatures showed who had moved each bundle and who received it. Yue noticed his breathing slow as the question became something he could answer with a page. Suspicion had made him rehearsed; a specific request made him useful.

canal_p04_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_009.text: The canal register's listed bundle was present, but its outer label named timber deliveries. Pei's toll-book reference appeared on an interior cover visible without untying the whole stack. An Ru checked the receiving number, stitching and page range, then requested the bundle for the comparison room. The clerk brought a carrying board because one corner of the wrapper had weakened. Yue held the door rather than grabbing the book. The original was close enough that excitement could now damage it.

canal_p04_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_010.text: Inside the comparison room, a skylight put a bright square over the table and left the rest in cool shadow. An Ru placed the register at the edge of that light, where the wrapper's condition could be seen without heating under direct sun. The junior clerk called the building conservator before they opened a damp-looking outer fold. Yue waited with her hands on her knees. The book had survived twenty-four years. It did not owe her an instant reveal because she had spent a morning traveling.

canal_p04_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_011.text: The conservator found old staining on the wrapper but no active wet layer in the protected register. She replaced the weakened support fold and recorded the condition before allowing ordinary page turning. Her tools were paper boards, clean brushes and patience. Yue thought of the green relay trace at the keeper's bench. This work had no visible glow. It would preserve a sentence through the afternoon just as surely as the other apparatus preserved a bounded physical route.

canal_p04_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_012.text: The first opened leaf described the founding timber advance in two separate clauses. One assigned a fixed share of actual toll receipts to repay the loan. The other established seasonal maintenance work so the repaired banks could remain usable. They appeared beside each other because both supported the canal, not because unpaid money extended every work turn indefinitely. Yue copied the headings before reading the amounts. Han's transcription had begun below the second heading, where the seasons' limit had already disappeared.

canal_p04_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_013.text: The heading named four annual maintenance seasons, sixty days in each. Renewal required a new household meeting after the final season, with tasks and replacements named anew. Birth, marriage or death did not renew it. Tian's successor list had no place in that instruction. An Ru read the passage twice while Yue watched the clean lower strokes of the last line. The words were plain. Their plainness made all the later anger feel more painful, because no ancient riddle had required anyone to enlarge them.

canal_p04_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_014.text: Yue wanted to send the heading to Tian immediately. An Ru asked her to finish the source comparison first. The register's seal matched the public receiving copy, and its page range joined the surviving transcription at the expected line. The proof came through that chain, not through how satisfying the sentence sounded. Yue wrote the full paragraph with its neighboring terms intact. A clipped triumphant extract could repeat the same habit that had created Han's incomplete working copy.

canal_p04_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_015.text: The bed-title clause remained public passage property under the founding charter. The loan secured only the specified unused timber stock and its toll share, excluding the watercourse, banks and persons using them. Han's north loading plot was separately described and genuinely private. An Ru laid the boundary plan beside the clause. It matched Luo's surviving stones better than the auction's broad white paint. The canal could not become Han's sale lot because his own founding document had never given it to his family.

canal_p04_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_016.text: The original repayment schedule showed one hundred twenty-eight copper returned in cash and thirty-two credited for unused timber delivered back to the lender. Together they made the one hundred sixty already acknowledged in Han's three receipts. The remaining eighty was real. The unused-stock security had been discharged through that returned timber; the permitted toll share remained. Yue was relieved the numbers did not erase his mother's contribution. She could bring him a narrower valid claim instead of treating a corrected title as cancellation of everything he feared losing.

canal_p04_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_017.text: The labor pages did not provide the same immediate closure. Several season totals were clear; others referred to replacement entries stored in the toll book. A final certificate stated the council had accepted completion, but its attached work schedule was elsewhere. An Ru would verify the referenced records before declaring every individual contribution settled. Yue thought of the widow's fourteen-day receipt and its earlier twelve. The original had answered duration and title. Completed work still deserved the separate careful accounting its people had actually done.

canal_p04_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_018.text: An Ru dictated a short provisional source note for the canal council: the pledge was bounded to four seasons; successor labor and canal-bed title were excluded; the monetary toll claim required its preserved separate repayment terms. She left the completion references for tomorrow's follow-up. The junior clerk made two certified copies under the archive's normal process. Yue asked to add the exact page range to both. Her earlier public mistake had taught her that a useful answer should give another reader somewhere specific to disagree.

canal_p04_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_019.text: While the copies dried, the schoolgirl brought the persimmons and announced that she had finally found a public use for her father's excessive generosity. Yue took one and nearly broke a tooth on its hard outer edge. An Ru showed her how to soak it in warm tea. The clerk laughed behind his hand. After hours of careful original comparison, Yue had been defeated by a snack. She let the small embarrassment make the room ordinary again.

canal_p04_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_020.text: The archivist's receiving ledger showed why the register had stayed here. The canal requested its return during a second roof repair, but the keeper then postponed transport because the lower boat route was unsafe. No later collector was named. The archive kept it as recorded custody, not as forgotten property it could dispose of. Pei's memory had preserved the transfer and lost the postponement. Yue copied both steps, giving the absent retired clerk a fuller history rather than a sentence accusing her of losing the book.

canal_p04_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_021.text: At the midday break, An Ru took Yue to a courtyard where water dripped from a newly repaired gutter. A mason was checking the ordinary outlet while two apprentices argued about whose turn it was to carry debris. The canal's trouble had become a familiar shape inside another public workplace. Yue admitted she wished the found heading could make everyone reasonable at once. An Ru asked whether Yue herself had become reasonable immediately after being corrected. They ate their softened persimmons in a silence that supplied the answer.

canal_p04_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_022.text: Han's buyer had an archive agent waiting for the provisional copy. The man asked whether the missing labor value made the conditional sale automatically void. An Ru said the buyer's private agreement required its own reading under the verified title limits. The archive could certify the found source, not decide a separate remedy by enthusiasm. He accepted the copy and requested the page range. Yue recognized a commercial question that might become useful to the canal if its answer stayed within what the book actually established.

canal_p04_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_023.text: The agent asked Yue whether Han knowingly hid the heading. She described the incomplete transcription, back-page attachment note and original register's recorded custody. Those facts explained how a missing line persisted; they did not establish his knowledge before the comparison. His enlarged successor list and continued title claim would still need correction now. The agent seemed disappointed by the narrower answer. Yue understood that appetite. A person who had just found an important truth could still be tempted to make it tell a more satisfying story than it knew.

canal_p04_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_024.text: Pei's recollection arrived in the packet with one line that contradicted the original: she remembered five seasons, counting the first emergency winter separately. The heading counted that winter within four. An Ru preserved her wording beside the dated schedule. Yue would read the difference to Pei when they returned. The retired clerk had been right about an end and wrong about its exact count. Her valuable testimony did not need to become perfect before it could help find a valid document.

canal_p04_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_025.text: Late in the afternoon, the conservator opened the companion work bundle. Its first page had old water damage at the edge, and a repair slip identified displaced entries now copied into a toll volume. The widow's reference matched one of those replacements. Tomorrow they could follow the copied schedule without forcing the fragile original to reveal erased strokes. Yue felt the search change direction again. The register had supplied the bounded terms; ordinary transfers and repairs would have to show how the work had actually finished.

canal_p04_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_026.text: Wei Xiu came to the archive courtyard before her return turn. The pilot could carry a certified provisional note to Luo that evening, while Yue and An Ru stayed for the next scheduled comparison. Yue sealed the note without adding a private message calling the dispute won. Tian would hear the ending clause soon enough. Han would hear the valid monetary claim beside it. The same boat would carry both, which seemed a fairer use of its dry box than her first excited impulse.

canal_p04_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_027.text: The overnight room stood above a public tea shop, with a narrow bed and a window overlooking the archive roofs. An Ru had booked two ordinary places under the scheduled comparison expense. Yue bought her own supper from her work pay and wrote the day's actual source findings before the street lamps dimmed. She kept the family names out of her letter home. The book had changed other people's future tasks; it had not made their private grief her entertaining travel story.

canal_p04_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_028.text: At dawn, Yue woke to a cart wheel rattling over stones and thought for a moment she was above the canal flour store. An Ru was already comparing yesterday's copied references. The second archive afternoon would examine the final completion schedule, original repayments and the precise transfer path. The ward clerk also offered a public boundary-plan comparison. Each could strengthen a different part of the coming hearing. Yue had to choose where her own careful work would make the largest useful difference today.

canal_p04_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_029.text: The original four-season heading lay behind a fresh protective sheet. Its promise had an end, while the eighty-copper toll balance still required repayment. Yue could help trace completed labor, compare the returned-timber credit or align the public boundary plan with Luo's actual-use map. An Ru would lead the remaining comparisons. The choice would determine which people Yue could answer directly when she returned, after a night spent imagining how differently each of them would receive the same found page.

choices.text: Trace completed household labor and its receiving references.
Compare the cash payments and returned-timber credit.
Align the public plan with Luo's current boundary observations.

canal_p04_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_030.text: The completion bundle used a column for workdays and another for workers attending. Yue nearly added both before the clerk pointed to their headings. A two-person half-day could appear as one completed day and two names. The grand seasonal total counted time, not bodies. She copied the units beside every number. The old successor list had treated people as service quantities; even a careful review could repeat that mistake if it preferred the larger-looking column.

canal_p04_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_031.text: The first season's sixty days were entered across bank clearing, timber placement and a temporary spill watch. Several households supplied no labor because illness kept them home; others took replacement turns. The pledge had organized a shared seasonal total rather than identical demands from every door. Yue thought of the widow's fourteen days and understood how one family's contribution could exceed an expected share without making the neighboring family permanently indebted to its descendants.

canal_p04_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_032.text: A margin note identified a paid specialist's inspection separately from household turns. Bao's predecessor had checked the new gates under a timber-work contract. His two inspection days were not deducted from the sixty household maintenance days. The clerk said later copies sometimes lost that distinction because both appeared in the same season book. Yue kept the two categories separate in her extract. The original labor promise had limits, and the original paid craft had its own account.

canal_p04_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_033.text: The second season's sheet bore a correction to a family name. A daughter married between the work and its acknowledgment, so the receipt used one household and the compiled schedule another. The adjoining transfer note linked them. Yue had expected a correction to conceal trouble. Here it preserved a person's changing life without inventing another worker. She copied the link and left both names visible. A clean single-name version would have made the completed days harder to recognize.

canal_p04_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_034.text: The third season's accepted total referred to a missing lower slip. Its amount survived in the clerk's signed compilation, but the original work description did not. An Ru asked Yue to flag that gap rather than replace it with a likely task from the neighboring lines. The certificate established administrative acceptance. It did not let them reconstruct every movement of a body more than twenty years later. Yue wrote the precise uncertainty in the margin, where it could travel with the useful total.

canal_p04_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_035.text: The fourth season held the widow's household reference. Twelve days appeared on the first acknowledgment; two later replacement days joined them before the final sixty-day certificate. The earlier copy from the tea tin and the damp fourteen-day original now matched their respective points in that sequence. The missing neighbor's exterior number remained readable in this book. Yue copied it for the canal clerk, knowing the widow might prefer to recover that person's name as much as recover the count.

canal_p04_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_036.text: A final page accepted the four seasonal totals and discharged the four-season maintenance pledge. It did not cancel the monetary loan. The wording was unmistakable, yet An Ru wanted the canal's receiving copy compared before announcing the certificate as an uncontested present record. The archive copy's chain was sound; the households deserved an opportunity to correct attribution. Yue wrote a provisional finding that the collective pledge had been accepted as complete, with individual schedule checks still listed.

canal_p04_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_037.text: The junior clerk asked why individual attribution mattered if no future duty survived. Yue thought of the widow's husband and the sailmaker who had kept his mother's acknowledgment beside her needles. Their work was part of how families remembered themselves. Correcting an inherited demand should not erase the people who once carried the beams. The clerk nodded and added space in the extract for offered household corrections. Legal release and remembered contribution could be separate useful outcomes.

canal_p04_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_038.text: An Ru compared Yue's labor extract with the untouched original while the clerk read the numbers. One line transposed a reference digit. Yue corrected it before certification and kept the working error on her private sheet. The mistake would have sent tomorrow's messenger to the wrong household. She could see how easily an entire later story might begin from that tiny copied certainty. The corrected reference would now guide a real doorstep visit, rather than making another absent family seem unwilling to answer.

canal_p04_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_039.text: At the courtyard table, Yue explained the provisional completion finding to An Ru while the timber-credit and boundary comparisons finished. The returned stock credit matched Han's old receipt; the common bed and seasonal spill remained excluded from his loan security. Her own work could now answer why four seasonal totals were accepted and where individual references still needed comparison. Tomorrow's receiver walk would carry those questions back to people who had lived beneath the numbers.

canal_p04_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_040.text: The returned-timber receipt named two unused beams at sixteen copper each. Their issue marks matched the founding delivery schedule. The lender had accepted them back and credited thirty-two against the advance, as Han's receipt stated. Yue traced the marks without touching the original fold. The beams themselves were long gone. Their recorded return still mattered because the loan's unused-stock security could not be treated as if those same timbers remained available for a second collection.

canal_p04_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_041.text: The founding material account included freight and handling, not timber price alone. Han's mother had advanced the full two hundred forty under the agreed package. Yue could not reduce the valid balance by deciding that the wood looked cheaper in today's market. An Ru pointed to the accepted delivery notes and matching council signatures. The original price might have been burdensome, but this comparison was establishing the actual transaction rather than rewriting an old bargain through present irritation.

canal_p04_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_042.text: Two later cash receipts credited sixty-four each. They were compiled payments over earlier profitable periods, not promises that every later month produced the same surplus. A bridge diversion and rising maintenance costs had reduced the canal's net toll income. The remaining eighty persisted under the actual-receipts term without creating a right to command household labor again. Yue copied the payment dates and term together. A bare balance could seem like twenty-four years of deliberate refusal if its collection conditions disappeared.

canal_p04_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_043.text: The clerk brought a private supplier's offered countercopy of the returned beams. Its date differed by one day because it recorded unloading, while the lender's receipt recorded acceptance after inspection. Both named the same marks and amount. Yue had begun looking for disagreement as if disagreement always meant fraud. Here the two dates described two different acts. She wrote those acts above the dates before comparing them, allowing a mundane delivery sequence to remain mundane.

canal_p04_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_044.text: The unused-stock clause identified only the original marked surplus, not future gate timber or every movable thing on the bank. Its return had discharged that security. The permitted toll share still supported the eighty-copper claim. An Ru asked Yue to read the sentence to the buyer's archive agent without adding victory to it. The agent copied it carefully. The conditional canal sale had lost another supposed asset while the surviving monetary obligation became more precisely defined.

canal_p04_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_045.text: Han's mother had signed the timber credit with a crowded uneven mark. The archivist did not certify handwriting from its resemblance alone. The public receiving copy carried the same issue numbers, amount and witnessed acceptance, providing a separate transaction match. Yue liked the mark because it looked like a person trying to finish work with cold hands. She kept that feeling in her private notes. The financial finding rested on the matched records, not on the affection the ink invited.

canal_p04_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_046.text: A letter stored with the receipts asked the council to protect a household whose father was ill rather than demand its missing maintenance turn. The lender had accepted another household's replacement within the fixed seasonal total. Han had remembered his mother as a woman whose sacrifice entitled her descendants to loyalty. This small surviving request showed another part of her practice. Yue obtained an approved excerpt of the relevant administrative instruction, leaving its private clinical detail covered.

canal_p04_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_047.text: An Ru warned Yue against carrying that letter as a moral weapon. It could help explain the original handling of replacement work. It did not prove Han should possess his mother's temperament or forgive the remaining balance. Yue admitted she had already imagined reading it to make him ashamed. The archivist handed her the narrower certified terms instead. A useful fact could become cruelly convenient when somebody tried to use it as a substitute for a difficult current bargain.

canal_p04_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_048.text: The cash and stock credits totaled one hundred sixty, leaving eighty under the original monetary agreement. The returned-stock security was discharged. The remaining claim could be assigned only within its actual toll-receipts terms. Yue wrote those findings in a form Han could check against the same references. He would dislike parts of it and recognize others. The comparison had given her a truthful answer to his ledger, rather than an answer designed only to satisfy the households who opposed his sale.

canal_p04_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_049.text: At the courtyard table, Yue explained the payment sequence while the labor and boundary comparisons finished. The four-season maintenance pledge had a recorded completion certificate needing its receiving references checked; the bed and spill remained outside private title. Her own work could now show why eighty remained and why returned timber could not become another claim on the gate stock. Tomorrow's receiver walk would carry those distinct findings back to the creditor and households together.

canal_p04_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_050.text: The public plan was larger than the table. Yue and the ward clerk supported its ends on clean boards while An Ru checked the receiving number. The canal bed appeared in pale blue, the private north plot in ochre and the seasonal spill in an uncolored margin. Han's painted sale line crossed all three. The original had not ignored the empty-looking hollow. It had described its flood function in a separate clause instead of pricing it as permanent dry land.

canal_p04_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_051.text: The survey's measurements used the old willow stone as one anchor. That stone had moved after erosion, exactly as Luo observed. The plan could guide a renewed survey but could not restore today's coordinates by insisting the old ground stayed still. Yue copied the measured distances and the anchor condition together. A disputed boundary would need current physical comparison. The original title scope was clear even while one edge's present location required ordinary work beside the water.

canal_p04_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_052.text: The common towpath had a passage corridor rather than an unlimited width. Doorsteps, washing places and loading interruptions were covered by separate use agreements. Yue thought of the widow's new rack and the receiver's red board. The plan did not supply a universal answer that made every household arrangement unlawful. It supplied a shared route whose actual clearance had to be maintained. She marked the corridor and left the local permissions beside it instead of swallowing them into the blue bed color.

canal_p04_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_053.text: The private crane's old crossing right had been approved for one season and required renewal after that. An archive note showed later renewals for limited cargo turns, with a gap in the most recent years. Bao's new reduced swing avoided the public path entirely, making the expired crossing less urgent to present operations. Han still deserved the actual record of his earlier permissions. Yue copied their dates without pretending a current defect made all past use unauthorized.

canal_p04_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_054.text: The seasonal spill clause required keeping the entrance available for high flow while ordinary bank use continued in dry periods. It did not authorize filling the hollow for permanent storage. It also named households below the fork as affected receivers whose drainage had to be reviewed when diversion changed. Those names were older than the current bank list. Yue requested the receiving district's latest public map. The flood path's apparently empty ground led toward people they had not yet met.

canal_p04_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_055.text: The ward clerk wanted to color the spill as common property and be done. An Ru showed him the clause's distinction: its use right protected diversion, while parts of the ground had household cultivation rights in dry seasons. A canal commons could require a flood path without owning every crop growing beneath it. Yue copied the affected-receiver condition. The coming repair would need more than a declaration that Han could not sell the hollow. It would need people downstream to help define what safe use now meant.

canal_p04_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_056.text: An older map showed an orchard ridge narrowing the lower channel after a bank slip. The surviving title plan predated that change. Luo's proposed restoration of the old diversion might therefore send water differently from the founding design. Yue had arrived hoping the original would answer every present question. The map gave her a more demanding answer: some rights remained, while the physical route those rights described had changed. Bao's gate repair would need measurements beyond the familiar lock.

canal_p04_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_057.text: The clerk copied the downstream receiver names without carrying their old household debts into the public map extract. Yue asked for current contact addresses through the receiving district rather than assuming descendants stayed in the same houses. The map's historical usefulness could otherwise recreate Tian's successor problem in another form. An Ru approved the narrower request. They would find actual people before asking them to accept a restored flood path on the strength of names nearly a quarter century old.

canal_p04_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_058.text: Yue compared her boundary extract against Luo's field sketch. The private plot fit the genuine wharf goods; the canal bed stayed excluded from sale; the shifted willow anchor and changed lower channel remained marked for current survey. The seasonal spill's affected-receiver clause became a new task rather than a footnote. She wrote its address request at the top of the return packet. The book had changed tomorrow's map walk as well as the next legal hearing.

canal_p04_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_059.text: At the courtyard table, Yue explained the boundary comparison while the labor and payment checks finished. The four-season pledge had a completion certificate to verify; eighty copper remained under the toll term. Her own work could now show why private loading goods remained private and why the common diversion needed downstream people, not merely an old plan. Tomorrow's receiver walk would begin returning these findings to the canal, where every accurate clause still had to meet actual ground.

canal_p04_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_060.text: All three comparisons met on An Ru's table before the second afternoon ended. The four annual maintenance seasons had a recorded discharge; the remaining eighty belonged to the separate toll claim; the public bed and seasonal spill were excluded from sale. Several individual work references still needed the canal's receiving copy. Yue read the common note aloud without adding a conclusion about anybody's character. The archive had supplied valid terms. People at the canal would still have to decide what to do after hearing them.

canal_p04_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_061.text: The conservator wrapped the original register for continued archive custody. The canal could request its formal return after arranging a dry receiving place and safe transport, rather than treating Yue's satchel as a convenient cabinet. An Ru retained the approved certified extracts for the review. Yue watched the wrapper's worn edge disappear beneath a clean support. A book could remain where it was while its useful words finally moved. That seemed a more dignified ending than carrying it away as proof of victory.

canal_p04_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_062.text: Before they left, the junior clerk asked whether his temporary transfer list would be mentioned. An Ru included it in the source chain because it led from the old receiving index to the dry cabinet. He looked pleased and slightly afraid of being visible in an official account. Yue told him the note recorded a useful completed act, not responsibility for every later claim. He showed her the exit with a confidence he had lacked at the entrance.

canal_p04_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_063.text: The schoolgirl gave Yue two softened persimmons wrapped in clean paper. She said her father would send more next week whether anyone asked or not. Yue accepted the modest gift and wrote its sender's return message beside the parcel receipt rather than losing it inside the canal packet. Public urgency had a habit of making unrelated people wait. She wanted the girl to receive an answer about her ordinary life as carefully as Tian would receive the pledge's ending clause.

canal_p04_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_064.text: Wei Xiu arrived with the canal's first replies. Luo acknowledged the provisional source note and asked for the affected-receiver map references. Han requested a full readable extract of the monetary term before agreeing to any payment plan. Tian wrote only three words beneath the heading's reference: 'Read it here.' Yue held that scrap longer than the others. The seamstress wanted a voice in a room, not a distant reassurance that an archive somewhere had finally found her freedom.

canal_p04_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_065.text: The return boat carried a smaller packet than Yue's excitement had originally imagined. Its source references were complete; its conclusions were limited; its originals stayed in recorded custody. An Ru sat beside her rather than forward, letting the packet rest on the ordinary dry board between them. Wei Xiu asked whether anybody wanted ginger tea. Yue protested that the pilot was abusing a useful memory. The women laughed while the valley steps fell behind the boat.

canal_p04_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_066.text: At the first ordinary landing, the family who sent persimmons asked whether their daughter had received them. Wei Xiu handed over her reply. The father read it twice and promised to send fewer next time, a promise his wife plainly distrusted. Yue watched their argument resume its affectionate familiar shape. The boat had carried proof of an expired labor pledge and proof that a girl still had too much dried fruit. Both replies deserved the right doorstep.

canal_p04_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_067.text: Farther downriver, a loaded cart waited on the bank because the small ferry's axle pin had slipped. Wei Xiu kept her mail schedule but passed the keeper an ordinary spare pin from her boat's maintenance box, logging its issue and replacement request. She could offer a specific object without promising to repair the whole crossing. Yue helped the keeper compare its size from the safe bank before the mail boat moved on. The day's found terms had not made ordinary mechanical work stop appearing.

canal_p04_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_068.text: The river grew restless near a narrow bend. Wei Xiu changed her approach after reading the actual eddies, not yesterday's easy route. An Ru steadied the packet while Yue kept the free rope clear of her feet. They passed under ordinary control and reached calm water beyond. The change cost a few minutes. Yue thought of the shifted willow stone and older flood map. A correct record could preserve a right without giving a pilot permission to ignore today's river.

canal_p04_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_069.text: An Ru asked Yue how she would read the expired pledge to Tian. Yue began with the clean ending sentence. The archivist asked what would come next. The monetary claim, current repair work and household attribution checks would still remain. Yue realized she had been imagining Tian's relief as if it concluded their relationship's difficult part. The seamstress would continue having preferences, anger and ordinary bills. A fair answer should leave her a person after it released her from a list.

canal_p04_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_070.text: At the canal mouth, Han's private wharf stood quiet beneath its secured beam. The reduced-load test had passed after the ordinary support repair, according to Bao's posted note. Normal loading would resume in smaller portions with the new arc. The public bank wall carried none of that private platform's load. Yue could see the changed geometry before hearing its explanation. While the archive found words, people at the wharf had made wood obey a safer set of dimensions.

canal_p04_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_071.text: Tian waited at the lower landing with Pei and the widow. She asked Yue to read the heading before anything else. Yue read the full paragraph, including the four annual maintenance seasons and the need for a fresh meeting to renew future work. Tian stood still for a long time. Then she asked whether the copy could be taken to the two households who declined the meeting. Relief had made her think outward, toward people she had nearly treated as inconvenient absences.

canal_p04_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_072.text: Pei corrected the remembered fifth season herself after hearing the original schedule. The emergency winter belonged within the first annual period, not outside it. She looked embarrassed until the widow reminded her that her recollection had still helped find the end. The retired clerk accepted both facts. Yue gave her the broad-script extract, with the discrepancy preserved on its own note. A valuable witness could remain imperfect without becoming somebody the room should stop listening to.

canal_p04_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_073.text: Han came from the wharf after the others read. Yue showed him the original payment term and returned-stock credit before the bed-title clause. He checked the three repayment references against his own copies. The eighty remained. The labor and sale claims did not. He asked whether the council would pay the available twenty-four now. Luo said the next meeting would authorize its actual disbursement after the receiving copy matched, with the ninety-six repair reserve protected as planned.

canal_p04_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_074.text: The widow asked to find the neighbor whose two replacement days joined her husband's fourteen. The archive's exterior household number led to an older towpath address. Its current residents were strangers to the original work. An Ru would trace the receiving records rather than assigning them the history merely because they occupied the door. Tian offered to walk with the message. The next day would return completed work to named people as carefully as the old notice had assigned work to names without asking.

canal_p04_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_075.text: Bao brought the gate guide's measurements while Han still held the monetary extract. The timber binding had an ordinary repair plan; the seasonal spill now required a wider downstream survey. Han asked whether postponing the spill would keep trade uncertain through the review. Luo said filling it would create a worse uncertainty they could not responsibly price. The question remained practical and contentious. The found heading had removed one invalid bargain without making every necessary new bargain easy.

canal_p04_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_076.text: The evening meeting agreed to send the certified terms to all twenty-eight current households, including absent families at their actual receiving addresses. No household's answer would be replaced by its neighbor's approval. The council would record the old collective discharge after comparing the public receiving schedule. Han's valid monetary claim would receive its own payment proposal. Yue watched Tian volunteer to deliver two nearby copies, a bounded act she chose after learning that a broader inherited act could not be required.

canal_p04_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_077.text: At the keeper's hearth, Luo gave Yue a bowl and asked which part of the original had surprised her most. Yue said the lender's accepted replacement turns and returned timber made Han's mother's history less rigid than the notice built from it. Luo said she remembered the woman laughing at a crooked boat pole. People became stiff in their descendants' defenses. Yue ate while thinking about the stories she told herself of her own mother, and whether love sometimes needed room to discover another ordinary detail.

canal_p04_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p04_078.text: Tomorrow's receiver walk would follow the completed-work references through the bank's actual households and old toll counter. Han would bring his copies; Tian would bring the messages people had chosen to answer; Pei would compare the receiving schedule without carrying the register herself. The canal's original four seasons had an end. Its present eight weeks still held a gate, a downstream map and a creditor who could no longer sell what he had never owned. Yue left the extract at the clerk's dry table and went upstairs.
